name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
history: Denver's first Catholic church, St. Mary's of 1860, was so poor it nailed canvas over the window openings. A cathedral was planned from 1880, but financial panics in 1893 and 1907 delayed it. Construction began in 1901, finished in 1911, and the cathedral was dedicated in 1912. It became a basilica in 1979.
arch: French Gothic Revival in granite and limestone, with twin spires facing Colfax Avenue. It seats 895.
features: Its twin spires are a Capitol Hill landmark.
Pope John Paul II celebrated Mass here during World Youth Day in 1993.

look.d: The spires rise over Colfax Avenue near the Colorado State Capitol.
Stained glass fills the great window of the French-style front.

fun: Denver's first church had canvas instead of glass in its windows.
journal: Gold Rush town to Gothic spires in fifty years. Canvas windows to stained glass.

quiz.q: What did Denver's first church use for windows?
